report.title: Every script, shipped or fix-touched, executed by all three real interpreters
report.question: Do the scripts actually run under the interpreters that will invoke them? Take the union of shipped scripts and scripts touched by any fix, execute each under PowerShell 7, Git Bash and real WSL bash, and answer: which fail on which interpreter, and is the cause line endings, quoting, path conversion, or a missing coreutil? A Git Bash syntax check is not evidence about strict Linux bash, which is exactly why the union is executed under all three rather than checked under one.
report.answer: Shipped-script union size is 60 under scripts/ and release/platforms/. crlf.note: CRLF fixture is exec'd via shebang under wsl-bash so the kernel sees 'bash\r'. Git Bash arm uses the igncr stand-in because MSYS is absent.

posix_path.note: MSYS Git Bash rewrites POSIX paths when calling Windows programs. On this Linux host the argument is received unchanged.

sections.1: Declared interpreter must be explicit in the launcher; implicit is a defect.
sections.3: Agent-written CRLF breaks real bash; Git Bash often tolerates the same bytes.
sections.8: POSIX-looking absolute paths are the Git Bash path-conversion trigger.
sections.10: Apostrophes break inlined command bodies; invoke the script by PATH.
